content_voiceover: Hemoglobin E is worth knowing cold, because it is the most common structural hemoglobin variant in the world after sickle hemoglobin, endemic across Southeast Asia, especially Cambodia, Thailand, and Vietnam. The molecular lesion is a beta 26 lysine to glutamate substitution. On its own, HbE is synthesized at a slightly reduced rate and is mildly unstable, but critically it does not significantly shorten red cell lifespan by itself, so homozygous HbE or HbE trait alone is usually mild or asymptomatic. The reason HbE behaves like a thalassemia gene rather than a pure structural variant is that the point mutation also creates an abnormal splice site, reducing normal beta E messenger RNA, that is the mechanistic link to thalassemia phenotypes. The clinical spectrum widens dramatically when HbE is co-inherited in trans with a true beta thalassemia mutation, HbE over beta zero or HbE over beta plus, because now there is a genuine chain imbalance, and HbE over beta zero thalassemia can look clinically identical to beta thalassemia major. The table shows this spectrum practically by transfusion requirement and age of presentation, group 1 patients never need transfusion and present around age 16, while group 5 patients require transfusion from as early as age 1, essentially transfusion dependent thalassemia. And just like other thalassemia syndromes, co-inherited alpha thalassemia is protective, reducing the globin chain imbalance and improving the anemia.
keypoints: HbE: β26 Lys→Glu, most common Hb variant in Southeast Asia
HbE alone (trait or homozygous): mild — does not significantly shorten RBC lifespan
HbE/β0-thalassemia can mimic β-thalassemia major clinically
Co-inherited α-thalassemia improves anemia by reducing chain imbalance
Severity spectrum spans age 1 (transfusion-dependent) to age 16 (never transfused)
keypoint_voiceover: Key facts on HbE. It is a beta 26 lysine to glutamate substitution and the most common hemoglobin variant across Cambodia, Thailand, and Vietnam. Alone, HbE trait or homozygous HbE is mild, because the variant does not meaningfully shorten red cell survival. The danger comes when HbE pairs with a true beta thalassemia mutation, HbE over beta zero thalassemia in particular can present just like beta thalassemia major. As with other thalassemias, co-inherited alpha thalassemia softens the phenotype. And clinically the spectrum is wide, some patients never need a transfusion and present in their teens, while others are transfusion dependent from infancy.
